title: Gravity and Archive
premise: Rosalind Hartwell, a clone created to inherit her original's unfinished murder investigation, arrives on Meridian Station to find the colony's life-support quietly failing and its administrators falsifying records to hide it. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew biologically aged backward by cryogenic anomaly, the station's council sees salvation: the Halcyon's sleepers could repopulate dying Earth colonies — but only half can be revived before the power fails. Rosalind discovers her original was murdered because she found the same falsified logs, and that the man she is falling for, Halcyon's navigator Elias Voss, aged backward into complicity he doesn't remember committing. In the end Rosalind broadcasts the archive to every colony, forcing an open vote on who wakes, sacrifices her legal claim to justice for a public one, and chooses Elias even as duty demands she wake the sleepers instead.
about_author: Coral Hartwell is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing decommissioned orbital habitats before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about records, memory, and the people institutions leave behind.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She docks at Meridian Station carrying her original's case files and her face, and is greeted with polite hostility by Administrator Corven. The colony is quieter than the manifests claim. Emotional beat: uncanny displacement — walking through a life someone else already lived.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Reviewing her original's notes, she finds air-scrubber maintenance logs that stop mid-year and resume with suspiciously identical phrasing. A technician warns her off the lower decks. Beat: first cold dread that the murder was administrative, not personal.

chapters.title: Lower Decks
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She descends into sealed sections where families live off rationed oxygen nobody officially counts. A girl named Iyo shows her a hidden garden fed by stolen power. Beat: the colony's forgotten humanity versus its polished upper levels.

chapters.title: Signal from the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Aboard the returning ship Halcyon, navigator Elias Voss wakes to instruments reading impossible telemetry: his own body is twenty years younger than his memories. The crew celebrates survival while he privately catalogs what feels wrong. Beat: disoriented wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Everyone Younger Than Their Crimes
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The Halcyon docks; crowds cheer the miraculously young crew. Rosalind meets Elias and recognizes him from her original's witness list — a man who testified, then vanished. Beat: attraction shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Decrypted files reveal her original had proof Meridian's council diverted life-support funds to a private evacuation ark. The last entry names a witness: E. Voss. Beat: grief for a self she never met, and a terrible new lead.

chapters.title: The Council's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Corven. The administrator calculates remaining power against population and concludes only half the sleepers aboard Halcyon can be revived. He begins drafting criteria disguised as medical triage. Beat: chillingly reasonable corruption.

chapters.title: Cryobay Confessions
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias searches his own aged-backward memory for the testimony he gave and finds gaps shaped like editing. He approaches Rosalind, offering cooperation he may not be able to trust. Beat: two investigators circling a truth one of them may have buried in himself.

chapters.title: Iyo's Garden Burns
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The hidden lower-deck garden is 'reclaimed' by security; Iyo's family is relocated toward the failing sections. Rosalind realizes the triage list has already been written — the sleepers are simply its cover. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Archive of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She begins recording testimony from colonists the official record omits, building a parallel archive in defiance of her mandate. Elias helps, and the partnership turns tender. Beat: love kindling inside the work, guilt attached.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Under Rosalind's questioning, fragments surface: Elias didn't just testify — he carried the original's evidence, and lost it, or gave it up, or was made to. His youth makes every memory deniable. Beat: self-doubt as a weapon turned inward.

chapters.title: Corven's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Corven. The administrator offers Rosalind her original's rank, full access, and closure of the murder file if she endorses the revival criteria. He genuinely believes he is saving the most people possible. Beat: temptation framed as duty.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The council announces the selection publicly: genetic diversity scores, skill matrices, lottery residue. The crowd's relief at any plan drowns the question of who decided. Beat: horror at how easily arithmetic becomes consent.

chapters.title: The Murder Weapon Was a Signature
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Forensics on the original's final hours point to a coerced authorization — she was made to sign her own silence before dying. The signature matches a template still used by Corven's office. Beat: the case snaps into focus.

chapters.title: Elias Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Elias. A cryobay malfunction forces a manual revival drill, and the sensory echo cracks his memory open: he surrendered the evidence to save his crew from being stranded. Complicity and coercion entwined. Beat: shame, and the choice to confess anyway.

chapters.title: Power Failure
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The grid fails ahead of schedule; sections go dark, including the cryobays' backups. Corven accelerates the revival timeline to whatever half the power can now reach — fewer than half. Beat: the clock becomes a blade.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Using the station's ancient archive array, Rosalind transmits everything — the logs, the testimonies, the murder — to every colony in range, making secrecy impossible. Beat: terror and liberation; justice seized outside the law.

chapters.title: Vote Among the Dying
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief voices. Colonists and awakened crew argue in corridors and open channels; Iyo speaks for those never counted. An improvised referendum forms around the revival list. Beat: democracy arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The vote ratifies a new list built from the archive's testimony — the forgotten included — but power will fail before it completes. Someone must stay behind to manually sequence the bays. Beat: sacrifice made concrete.

chapters.title: Duty Is a Room With No Windows
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias volunteers for the sequencer room, arguing his backward life is borrowed anyway. Rosalind refuses to accept the logic of his erasure. Beat: love against duty at knife-point.

chapters.title: Gravity and Archive
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Climax: Rosalind takes the sequencer post herself, routing her own clone-body's legal identity as collateral so no one can reverse the vote; Elias holds the line beside her as the last bays cycle. Corven, exposed, chooses to help rather than be archived as the villain alone. Beat: the title's meaning fulfilled — what pulls us down, what we keep.

chapters.title: What We Kept
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epilogue voice. Power holds by margins; the chosen sleepers wake alongside colonists once uncounted. Rosalind closes her original's case not with an arrest but with a public record no one can sign away, and opens a new file titled with her own name. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
